payload.quote: While our analysis reveals a considerable influence of defaults (d = 0.68, 95% confidence interval = 0.53–0.83), we also discover substantial variation: the majority of default studies find positive effects, but several do not find a significant effect, and two even demonstrate negative effects.
payload.test: Refuted if the paper's base model in DefaultMetaAnalysisandPlots.Rmd, metafor::rma(Cohens_D, Variance_D, test = "t", data = defaultmetafull) (REML, metafor's default), fitted on all rows of defaultmetadata.csv, has k ≠ 58, or if its estimate or 95% CI limits, rounded half away from zero to two decimals, differ from 0.68 [0.53, 0.83], or its I², rounded half away from zero to two decimals, differs from 98.21% (p. 168). Inconclusive if the run stops, times out or does not converge, or gives no finite value for a compared figure.

scope.basis: Methods (p. 163): "we include studies regardless of their publication date"; "Our search concluded in May 2017". No earliest cutoff exists: 1993-01 marks only the earliest Year (1993) among the 58 included observations, from 55 studies in 35 articles, as the posted data record them; it is no study or eligibility date.

fidelity.basis: The paper's own model and data; ours is the rule: its printed figures must be reproduced, with 'substantial variation' read as the base model's I² of 98.21% (p. 168). The sentence's counts ('several' non-significant, 'two' negative) are not tested, as the paper gives no rule for them. A computational check with known targets; it tests no new sample.
